title: Pillows, Wet with Tears of Anguish
description: Pillows, Wet with Tears of Anguish in Tonic Solfa to STUTTGART, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Pierpont wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 794 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Morning Hymn for Family Worship”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to STUTTGART; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Pil-lows, wet with tears of an-guish, Couch-es, pressed in sleep-less woe, Where the sons of Be-lial lan-guish, Fa-ther, may we nev-er know!

lines: Pillows, wet with tears of anguish,
Where the sons of Belial languish,
For, the maddening cup shall never
To our thirsting lips be pressed,
But, our draft shall be, forever,
The cold water thou hast blessed.
This shall give us strength to labor,
This, make all our stores increase;
This, with thee and with our neighbor,
Bind us in the bonds of peace.
For the lake, the well, the river,
Do we now, to thee, the Giver,

licence: Public domain: John Pierpont died in 1866.
credits: Words by John Pierpont (1785–1866), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to STUTTGART by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
